months.key_festivals: Hindu New Year (Vikram Samvat), Chaitra Navratri, Gangaur, Ram Navami, Hanuman Jayanti, Mahavir Jayanti
Akshaya Tritiya, Buddha Purnima, Narasimha Jayanti, Ganga Saptami
Vat Savitri, Ganga Dussehra, Nirjala Ekadashi
Rath Yatra, Guru Purnima, Devshayani Ekadashi (Chaturmas begins)
Sawan Somvar, Hariyali Teej, Nag Panchami, Raksha Bandhan
Janmashtami, Hartalika Teej, Ganesh Chaturthi, Anant Chaturdashi, Pitru Paksha begins
Pitru Paksha ends, Sharad Navratri, Durga Puja, Dussehra, Sharad Purnima
Karwa Chauth, Ahoi Ashtami, Dhanteras, Diwali, Govardhan Puja, Bhai Dooj, Chhath, Dev Uthani Ekadashi, Tulsi Vivah, Kartik Purnima
Kalbhairav Jayanti, Vivah Panchami, Gita Jayanti (Mokshada Ekadashi)
Paush Putrada Ekadashi, Paush Purnima; Makar Sankranti (solar) falls at the Paush-Magh boundary
Vasant Panchami, Maghi Purnima, Maha Shivratri (Magh Krishna Chaturdashi in Amanta/southern reckoning)
Maha Shivratri (Purnimanta: Phalgun Krishna Chaturdashi), Holika Dahan, Holi

tithis.significance: First day of a paksha; good for starting new work
Auspicious for Bhai Dooj (Kartik Shukla Dwitiya)
Ganesh Chaturthi (Shukla), Sankashti Chaturthi (Krishna), Karwa Chauth
Nag Panchami, Vasant Panchami, Vivah Panchami
Durga Ashtami, Janmashtami, Sheetla Ashtami, Ahoi Ashtami
Ekadashi vrat (twice a month); Dev Uthani, Nirjala, Gita Jayanti
Maha Shivratri, Narak Chaturdashi, Anant Chaturdashi
Full moon (Shukla) or new moon (Krishna); Satyanarayan katha, Diwali, Pitru tarpan

festivals.significance: Marks the Sun's entry into Capricorn and the start of Uttarayan, the Sun's northward journey. A harvest festival and an especially auspicious time for charity and holy dips.
festivals.how_celebrated: Early holy dip, Surya arghya, daan of til, jaggery, khichdi and warm clothes, family feasts and kite flying.
festivals.traditional_foods: til-gud laddu, khichdi, gajak, pheeni, ghevar
festivals.muhurat_rule: Punya Kaal / Maha Punya Kaal after the Sankranti moment is best for snan and daan.
festivals.regional_notes: Jaipur and Rajasthan: huge kite-flying (patangbazi) day, called Sakraat; daan and feasts of ghevar/pheeni. Punjab: Maghi. Gujarat: Uttarayan. Tamil Nadu: Pongal.

dates.note: Sankranti moment on Jan 14; many rituals/snan on the morning of Jan 15.
Sun enters Makara on the evening of Jan 14; observed Jan 15 by many calendars.

rituals.title: Holy bath
rituals.description: Take a bath before sunrise, ideally with a few sesame seeds in the water or at a holy river.

rituals.title: Surya arghya
rituals.description: Offer water in a copper lota to the Sun with red flowers and chant Surya mantras.

rituals.title: Daan
rituals.description: Donate til, jaggery, khichdi ingredients, blankets and warm clothes to the needy.

rituals.title: Kite flying and food
rituals.description: Eat til-gud, khichdi and ghevar; fly kites with family.

festivals.significance: Punjabi winter-harvest festival celebrating the passing of the longest nights and the new crop.
festivals.how_celebrated: Evening bonfire with songs and dancing; popcorn, peanuts, revri and gajak are offered to the fire.
festivals.traditional_foods: revri, gajak, popcorn, peanuts, sarson da saag
festivals.regional_notes: Mainly Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and North India.

rituals.title: Bonfire
rituals.description: Gather around the bonfire at sunset, circle it and offer popcorn, peanuts, sesame and revri.

rituals.title: Dance and food
rituals.description: Perform bhangra and enjoy sarson da saag, makki di roti and sweets.

festivals.tithi: Thai Pongal (first day of Tamil month Thai)
festivals.significance: Tamil harvest festival thanking the Sun, nature and cattle.
festivals.how_celebrated: Rice is boiled with milk in a new pot until it overflows; kolam designs, sugarcane, and cattle worship (Mattu Pongal).
festivals.regional_notes: Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Tamil diaspora.

dates.note: Thai Pongal; some calendars list Jan 14.

rituals.title: Cooking Pongal
rituals.description: Boil milk and rice in a new pot in the courtyard and shout 'Pongalo Pongal' when it overflows; offer to the Sun on a banana leaf.

rituals.title: Mattu Pongal
rituals.description: Next day cattle are bathed, decorated and fed.

festivals.significance: Welcomes spring and honours Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, music and arts.
festivals.how_celebrated: People wear yellow, worship Saraswati with books and instruments, and children are introduced to writing (Vidyarambh).
festivals.muhurat_rule: Purvahna (forenoon) puja when Panchami is present.
festivals.regional_notes: Rajasthan and North India: yellow clothes and yellow food; Bengal: Saraswati Puja in schools; Punjab: kite flying.

rituals.title: Yellow setup
rituals.description: Wear yellow, clean the puja space and place the Saraswati image with books and instruments.

rituals.title: Saraswati puja
rituals.description: Offer yellow flowers, roli, haldi, kesari bhaat; keep pen and books for blessing.

rituals.title: Vidyarambh
rituals.description: Children are guided to write their first letters on rice or slate.

rituals.title: Prasad
rituals.description: Distribute kesari bhaat and boondi.

festivals.significance: The great night of Shiva, commemorating Shiva-Parvati's marriage and Shiva's cosmic dance. Devotees stay awake and fast.
festivals.how_celebrated: Night-long jagran, abhishek of the Shivling with water, milk, curd, honey and ghee, offering bel patra, chanting Om Namah Shivaya; four-prahar puja.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Nishita Kaal (midnight) puja; four prahar puja through the night.
festivals.regional_notes: Jaipur and Rajasthan: abhishek at Shiv temples and long queues; Ujjain Mahakaleshwar; Varanasi Kashi Vishwanath.

rituals.title: Fast and sankalp
rituals.description: Take sankalp in the morning; fast with fruits and water or fully nirjala.

rituals.title: First prahar abhishek
rituals.description: Bathe the Shivling with water and milk, offer bel patra and dhatura chanting Om Namah Shivaya.

rituals.title: Second to fourth prahar
rituals.description: Abhishek with curd (2nd), ghee (3rd) and honey (4th) as per the four-prahar tradition; keep a night-long jagran.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast next morning after sunrise with prasad.

festivals.significance: Commemorates the victory of devotion (Prahlad) over evil (Holika). The bonfire burns negativity.
festivals.how_celebrated: Community pyre is lit after puja with raw thread, grain ears, coconut and water; people circle the fire and take its ash.
festivals.muhurat_rule: After sunset during Pradosh Kaal on Purnima; avoid Bhadra Kaal.
festivals.regional_notes: Rajasthan/Haryana: badkule (cow-dung garlands) offered to the fire; Gujarat and Maharashtra also big.

dates.note: Purnima spans Mar 2-3; muhurat varies by city; verify for Jaipur.

rituals.title: Build the Holika pyre
rituals.description: In the locality build a pyre of wood and cow-dung cakes with the Holika-Prahlad effigy, a few days before.

rituals.title: Puja
rituals.description: At the muhurat worship Holika with roli, akshat, flowers, raw thread and water, circumambulate three or seven times.

rituals.title: Lighting
rituals.description: Light the pyre, offer coconuts, new wheat/gram ears and sweets to the fire.

rituals.title: Ash and prasad
rituals.description: Take a bit of ash or roasted grain home as prasad and apply the ash as tilak.

festivals.significance: Festival of colours celebrating spring, love and the triumph of good over evil.
festivals.how_celebrated: Playing with dry colours (gulal) and water, music, dance, meeting family and neighbours, special sweets.
festivals.traditional_foods: gujiya, thandai, malpua, dahi bhalla, mathri
festivals.regional_notes: Brij (Mathura, Vrindavan, Barsana: Lathmar Holi), Rajasthan (colourful and rural phag songs), West Bengal (Dol Jatra).

dates.note: Rangwali Holi on Mar 4 in North India; some calendars list Mar 3.
One source lists Mar 23.

rituals.title: Morning colours
rituals.description: Begin with a puja to Krishna-Radha or Narasimha and apply light tilak of gulal to elders.

rituals.title: Playing Holi
rituals.description: Play with dry colours and water with family and friends, with singing and dancing to Phag songs.

rituals.title: Evening meet
rituals.description: Wash up, wear new clothes, visit relatives and neighbours with gujiya and sweets.

festivals.significance: Worship of Sheetla Mata, protector from pox and heat-related illnesses, especially for children's health.
festivals.how_celebrated: Food is cooked the previous evening and eaten cold (basi bhojan); Sheetla Mata is offered the cold food with water and roli.
festivals.traditional_foods: rabri, dahi, roti, pua, cold kheer
festivals.muhurat_rule: Morning puja, no fresh cooking that day.
festivals.regional_notes: Big in Rajasthan (Sheetla Mata mela near Chaksu, Jaipur), Gujarat, UP and Haryana.

rituals.title: Cook the day before
rituals.description: Prepare all food (rabri, dahi, roti, pua) on Saptami evening; no fire on Ashtami.

rituals.title: Sheetla puja
rituals.description: At dawn visit the Sheetla Mata temple or puja corner and offer haldi, roli, water, neem leaves and the cold food.

rituals.title: Eat basi bhojan
rituals.description: Eat the cold food as prasad; sprinkle Sheetla Mata water on children.

samagri.name_hi: ठंडा / एक दिन पहले का बना भोजन (रोटी, खीर, दही)
samagri.name_en: Cold food cooked the day before

festivals.significance: Rajasthan's women-centred festival honouring Gauri (Parvati) and Isar (Shiva) for marital happiness and good husbands.
festivals.how_celebrated: Girls and women make and decorate clay idols, sing Gangaur songs, apply mehendi and fast; ends with a procession and visarjan.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Final-day puja on Chaitra Shukla Tritiya, evening procession.
festivals.regional_notes: Jaipur's royal Gangaur procession from the City Palace area; also Jodhpur, Udaipur, Bikaner; observed in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat too.

dates.note: Gangaur main day (Chaitra Shukla Tritiya).

rituals.title: Day 1 onward
rituals.description: From the day after Holi, girls bring fresh barley (jwara), clay Isar-Gauri idols and sing folk songs daily for 16-18 days.

rituals.title: Daily puja
rituals.description: Offer durva, flowers, haldi, kumkum and water to Gauri each morning.

rituals.title: Final day
rituals.description: Women dress in shringar with mehendi and offer ghevar and gunje; evening procession with decorated Gauri idols.

rituals.title: Visarjan
rituals.description: Immerse the idols or jwara in a pond or well with songs.

festivals.name_hi: हिंदू नववर्ष / विक्रम संवत् / उगादी / गुड़ी पड़वा
festivals.name_en: Hindu New Year (Vikram Samvat / Ugadi / Gudi Padwa)
festivals.significance: Chaitra Shukla Pratipada begins the lunar year (Vikram Samvat) and Chaitra Navratri; also Ugadi, Gudi Padwa and Cheti Chand in different regions.
festivals.how_celebrated: Panchang puja, neem-jaggery eaten, rangoli, flags (gudi) and home cleaning.
festivals.regional_notes: Maharashtra: Gudi Padwa; Karnataka/Telangana/AP: Ugadi; Sindhi: Cheti Chand; North India: Chaitra Navratri begins.

dates.note: Vikram Samvat 2083 begins.

rituals.title: Home cleaning
rituals.description: Clean the house, make rangoli and erect a gudi (flag) in some regions.

rituals.title: Panchang puja
rituals.description: Worship the new panchang, hear the year's forecast and eat neem-jaggery.

rituals.title: Start Navratri
rituals.description: Start Chaitra Navratri with Ghatasthapana.

festivals.significance: Nine days of Shakti worship in spring, ending with Ram Navami.
festivals.how_celebrated: Ghatasthapana, nine days of fasting and Durga path, Ashtami/Navami kanya pujan and havan.
festivals.traditional_foods: kuttu, singhara atta, sabudana, fruits, halwa-puri-chana
festivals.regional_notes: Strongest in North and West India; Rajasthan: devotees visit local Devi temples and fairs.

rituals.title: Ghatasthapana
rituals.description: Set up the kalash and jwara at the muhurat and light Akhand Jyot.

rituals.title: Nine-day worship
rituals.description: Worship the nine Durga forms daily with fasting and recite Durga Saptashati.

rituals.title: Ram Navami
rituals.description: Conclude with Navami havan, kanya pujan and Ram Navami puja.

samagri.name_hi: जवारे बोने का पात्र व मिट्टी
samagri.name_en: Pot and soil for jwara (barley sprouts)

samagri.name_hi: कन्या पूजन की भेंट (चुनरी, चूड़ी, फल)

festivals.significance: Birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, ideal of dharma.
festivals.how_celebrated: Midday birth puja (Ram Janma), Ramcharitmanas path, bhajans, processions and Ram darbar decoration.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Madhyahna (midday) is the Ram Janma moment.
festivals.regional_notes: Ayodhya's large celebrations; Rajasthan: Ram temples and Ram Navami shobha yatra.

dates.note: North India lists Mar 26; some South calendars Mar 27.

rituals.title: Morning bath and fast
rituals.description: Bathe, clean the puja corner and take the sankalp for the vrat.

rituals.title: Midday birth puja
rituals.description: At Madhyahna perform Ram Janma: abhishek of Ram Darbar with panchamrit, tulsi leaves, offering panakam/panjiri.

rituals.title: Path and bhajan
rituals.description: Recite Ramcharitmanas, Ram Raksha Stotra or Sundarkand and sing aarti.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast the next morning after Dashami with Brahmin or kanya bhojan.

festivals.significance: Birth anniversary of Mahavira, the 24th Jain Tirthankara, teaching ahimsa, truth and non-possession.
festivals.how_celebrated: Abhishek of Mahavira idols, rath yatra, charity, temple visits and sermons.
festivals.traditional_foods: sattvic food, no root vegetables for many families
festivals.regional_notes: Major in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra Jain communities (Jaipur has a large Jain population).

rituals.title: Janma kalyanak abhishek
rituals.description: Abhishek of Mahavira's idol with pure water and milk, followed by shanti-dhara.

rituals.title: Rath yatra
rituals.description: Procession with Mahavira's idol, charity and sermons.

festivals.significance: Birth anniversary of Hanuman, symbol of strength, devotion and service.
festivals.how_celebrated: Sunrise puja with sindoor chola, Hanuman Chalisa and Sundarkand path, offering laddu/boondi, bhandara.
festivals.regional_notes: Rajasthan: Mehandipur Balaji and Salasar Hanuman temples draw huge crowds; Tamil/Kerala/AP date differs.

rituals.title: Bath and sankalp
rituals.description: Bathe at dawn, clean the Hanuman murti or visit the temple.

rituals.title: Chola and puja
rituals.description: Apply jasmine oil with sindoor to the idol, offer red flowers, janeu, tulsi and laddu/boondi.

rituals.title: Path
rituals.description: Recite Hanuman Chalisa 11 times or Sundarkand and perform aarti.

rituals.title: Bhandara
rituals.description: Distribute prasad or hold a community bhandara.

festivals.significance: One of the most auspicious days of the year: anything started or given in charity is believed to bring lasting (akshaya) merit.
festivals.how_celebrated: Puja of Vishnu and Lakshmi, daan, buying gold or silver, starting new ventures; Jains mark Varshi Tap parana.
festivals.regional_notes: Rajasthan: Akha Teej is also an agricultural new-season day when farmers start work and read omens.

dates.note: Some South Indian calendars list Apr 20.

rituals.title: Morning bath
rituals.description: Bathe, wear clean clothes and take sankalp.

rituals.title: Lakshmi-Vishnu puja
rituals.description: Worship Vishnu and Lakshmi with tulsi, yellow flowers, barley and sattu.

rituals.title: Buy and give
rituals.description: Buy gold or silver (optional), start new work, and donate water pots, fans, sattu, barley or clothes.

rituals.title: Parana (Jain)
rituals.description: Jains break the year-long Varshi Tap with sugarcane juice.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: Celebrates the birth, enlightenment and nirvana of Gautama Buddha.
festivals.how_celebrated: Monastery and temple visits, meditation, charity, release of caged animals, readings of Buddhist texts.
festivals.regional_notes: Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Lumbini (Nepal), Sikkim and Ladakh.

rituals.title: Temple and meditation
rituals.description: Visit Buddha viharas, offer flowers, lamps and incense, and meditate.

rituals.title: Charity
rituals.description: Donate food and clothes, and observe the Panchsheel.

festivals.significance: Marks the descent of Ganga to earth; holy dip is said to cleanse sins.
festivals.how_celebrated: Early dip in Ganga or any river, Ganga aarti, daan of water vessels and sherbet.
festivals.regional_notes: Haridwar, Varanasi, Prayagraj and along the Ganga; also in Rajasthan at ponds and rivers.

dates.note: 2026 has an Adhik Maas; check sources.

rituals.title: Holy dip
rituals.description: Take a dip in the Ganga or any river at sunrise, chanting 'Om Namo Gange'.

rituals.title: Ganga aarti and daan
rituals.description: Light diyas and donate water pots, sherbet, fans and fruits.

festivals.significance: The strictest Ekadashi; fasting without water on this day is believed to equal observing all 24 Ekadashis.
festivals.how_celebrated: Vishnu puja, no food or water until next sunrise, daan of water pots, fans and sherbet.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Parana the next morning in the Dwadashi window.
festivals.regional_notes: Widely observed in North India; sherbet stalls (chhabeel) are common.

rituals.title: Sankalp
rituals.description: On Dashami eat lightly; on Ekadashi morning take sankalp to fast without water.

rituals.title: Vishnu puja
rituals.description: Worship Vishnu with tulsi leaves and yellow flowers and recite Vishnu Sahasranama.

rituals.title: Daan
rituals.description: Donate water pots, fans, clothes and sherbet.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast the next morning after sunrise in the parana window.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: Married women fast for their husband's long life, inspired by Savitri who won back Satyavan's life from Yama.
festivals.how_celebrated: Women worship the banyan tree, tie raw thread around it, circle it 7 or 108 times and read the Savitri-Satyavan katha.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Morning puja under the banyan tree.
festivals.regional_notes: North India observes it on Jyeshtha Amavasya; Maharashtra/Gujarat on Jyeshtha Purnima (Vat Purnima).

dates.note: Jyeshtha Amavasya (North India).

rituals.title: Fast prep
rituals.description: Prepare puja thali with fruits, kachcha soot, roli, chana and fan.

rituals.title: Vat puja
rituals.description: Offer water, roli, akshat and fruits to the banyan tree and tie raw thread 7 or 108 times around it.

rituals.title: Katha
rituals.description: Listen to the Savitri-Satyavan katha and pray for the husband's long life.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast after puja, and give a gift (bayana) to the mother-in-law.

festivals.significance: Annual chariot journey of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra from the Puri temple to Gundicha temple.
festivals.how_celebrated: Huge wooden chariots are pulled by devotees; bhajans and prasad distribution.
festivals.regional_notes: Puri (Odisha) main; ISKCON and Jagannath temples hold smaller yatras across India including Jaipur.

rituals.title: Chariot pulling
rituals.description: Pahandi rituals, then devotees pull the chariots of Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra.

rituals.title: Prasad
rituals.description: Distribute mahaprasad.

festivals.significance: Honours teachers and gurus; the day commemorates Vyasa, compiler of the Vedas and the Mahabharata.
festivals.how_celebrated: Pada puja of gurus, offering flowers and dakshina, satsang, reading scriptures; many also take a holy dip.
festivals.regional_notes: Observed by Hindus, Buddhists and Jains alike; Govardhan parikrama (Mathura) is popular.

rituals.title: Guru puja
rituals.description: Wash the guru's padukas or picture, offer flowers, fruits and dakshina and seek blessings.

rituals.title: Vyasa puja
rituals.description: Worship Veda Vyasa and read excerpts from Mahabharata or Vedas.

rituals.title: Seva
rituals.description: Do daan and satsang.

festivals.significance: Monsoon festival celebrating the reunion of Shiva and Parvati; women pray for marital happiness.
festivals.how_celebrated: Green clothes and bangles, mehendi, swings (jhula) decorated with flowers, folk songs and Teej Mata puja.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Morning to evening puja with Teej katha.
festivals.regional_notes: Jaipur's Teej procession carrying Teej Mata is famous; in Rajasthan Teej and Gangaur are the major women's festivals.

rituals.title: Green shringar
rituals.description: Apply mehendi and wear green sarees, bangles and a bindi; decorate the swing with flowers.

rituals.title: Teej Mata puja
rituals.description: Worship Shiva-Parvati or Teej Mata with sindoor, fruits and sweets and read the Teej katha.

rituals.title: Swings and songs
rituals.description: Women sing Teej songs on swings, gift sindhara to daughters and share ghevar.

festivals.significance: Worship of serpent deities; thanks and protection from snakes.
festivals.how_celebrated: Milk, haldi and flowers offered to snake images; no digging or cutting of the earth that day.
festivals.regional_notes: Maharashtra (Battis Shirala), Rajasthan (Nag temples) and South India.

rituals.title: Naga puja
rituals.description: Offer milk, haldi, roli and flowers to a snake image, a Naga murti or a snake pit and recite Naga mantras.

rituals.title: Observe restrictions
rituals.description: Avoid digging, cutting vegetables and frying on this day.

festivals.deity: भाई-बहन का पर्व (इंद्राणी-इंद्र, कृष्ण-द्रौपदी की कथा)
festivals.significance: Celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters; sisters tie a rakhi and brothers promise protection.
festivals.how_celebrated: Sister performs aarti, applies tilak, ties rakhi, offers sweets; brother gives a gift.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Rakhi to be tied outside Bhadra Kaal, usually in the afternoon.
festivals.regional_notes: Rajasthan: sisters also tie 'Lumba' rakhi to bhabhis; Maharashtra Narali Purnima; Gujarat Pavitropana.

dates.note: Some sources list Aug 27; check Bhadra Kaal for exact time.

rituals.title: Check Bhadra Kaal
rituals.description: Choose a rakhi time outside Bhadra Kaal.

rituals.title: Prepare the thali
rituals.description: Sister arranges the rakhi, roli, akshat, diya, sweets and coconut in a thali.

rituals.title: Tie rakhi
rituals.description: Tilak, tie rakhi on the right wrist, aarti and feed sweets; brother touches elders' feet if needed.

rituals.title: Gift and vow
rituals.description: Brother gives a gift and pledges protection.

festivals.significance: Birth of Lord Krishna at midnight in Mathura.
festivals.how_celebrated: Midnight abhishek of Laddu Gopal, jhula, bhajans, jhankis; next day Dahi Handi in Maharashtra.
festivals.regional_notes: Mathura-Vrindavan, Dwarka and Jaipur's Govind Dev Ji temple draw big crowds; Maharashtra: Dahi Handi.

dates.note: Smarta and Vaishnava observances can differ by a day.
Smarta/Vaishnava difference possible.

rituals.title: Fast and decorate
rituals.description: Fast during the day and decorate the home mandir with a jhula and flowers.

rituals.title: Midnight janma
rituals.description: At midnight bathe Laddu Gopal with panchamrit, dress him, place him in the jhula and (in many homes) cut a cucumber symbolically for the birth.

rituals.title: Bhog and aarti
rituals.description: Offer makhan-mishri, panjiri, tulsi and ring the bell; sing Krishna aarti.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast after the midnight puja; next day Dahi Handi and Nandotsav celebrations.

festivals.significance: Women observe a strict fast commemorating Parvati's penance to win Shiva.
festivals.how_celebrated: Sand or clay idols of Shiva-Parvati, night jagran, offering bel patra and shringar items to Parvati.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Pradosh or Pratahkala puja on Tritiya.
festivals.regional_notes: UP, Bihar, Nepal, Maharashtra, Rajasthan.

rituals.title: Sand idol
rituals.description: Prepare Shiva-Parvati idols from sand or clay, decorate with flowers and a chunri.

rituals.title: Evening puja
rituals.description: Offer bel patra, flowers and shringar items to Parvati and listen to the katha.

rituals.title: Night jagran
rituals.description: Women stay awake singing bhajans.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast next morning after puja.

festivals.significance: Birth of Lord Ganesha, remover of obstacles; prayers begin new ventures.
festivals.how_celebrated: Ganesha idol installed (pranpratishtha), daily aarti with modak and durva, immersion on a chosen day or Anant Chaturdashi.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Madhyahna Ganesh puja Muhurat on Chaturthi (avoid moon sighting on this night per tradition).
festivals.regional_notes: Maharashtra (Mumbai, Pune) is the biggest; Jaipur's Moti Doongri Ganesh Temple has special celebrations; Wednesdays are Ganesh days.

rituals.title: Bring the idol
rituals.description: Bring home an eco-friendly clay Ganesha, preferably facing east or north, on a decorated chowki.

rituals.title: Pranpratishtha
rituals.description: Install the idol with invocation (Avahan), offer a seat and wash the idol's feet symbolically.

rituals.title: Shodashopachar puja
rituals.description: Offer 16 upacharas: flowers, 21 durva, red hibiscus, sindoor, janeu, 21 modak, coconut; chant Atharvashirsha or Vakratunda mantra.

rituals.title: Daily aarti
rituals.description: Do morning and evening aarti with modak and fruits for 1.5, 3, 5, 7 or 10 days.

rituals.title: Visarjan
rituals.description: On the chosen day perform uttar puja and immerse the idol in a tank or artificial pond, chanting 'Ganpati Bappa Morya'.

festivals.significance: Vishnu Ananta puja and the final day of Ganesh immersion.
festivals.how_celebrated: Anant sutra (14-knot thread) tied after puja; Ganesh idols immersed with processions.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Morning puja, visarjan in the afternoon/evening.
festivals.regional_notes: Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja immersion; observed in Rajasthan with Ananta vrata.

rituals.title: Anant puja
rituals.description: Worship Lord Anant (Vishnu) with a kalash and tie a 14-knot Anant sutra on the right wrist (men) or left wrist (women).

rituals.title: Ganesh visarjan
rituals.description: Take a procession and immerse Ganesha idols in water bodies.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: Honours Vishwakarma, divine architect; workers, artisans and engineers worship their tools and machinery.
festivals.how_celebrated: Factory and workshop cleaning, tool worship, food distribution.
festivals.regional_notes: West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam and industrial belts.

dates.note: Solar date (Kanya Sankranti).

rituals.title: Tool worship
rituals.description: Clean tools, machines and workplaces, place Vishwakarma's image and offer flowers, roli and sweets.

rituals.title: Prasad
rituals.description: Share prasad and community meals with workers.

festivals.significance: Sixteen-day period to honour ancestors through tarpan, pind daan and shraddh.
festivals.how_celebrated: Shraddh on the tithi of the ancestor's death, tarpan with water and black sesame, feeding Brahmins and offering to cows, crows and dogs, charity.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Kutup Kaal / Rohina Kaal (midday) is the best time for shraddh.
festivals.regional_notes: Gaya (Bihar), Pushkar, Haridwar, Prayagraj are key pind daan places; Sarva Pitru Amavasya for unknown tithi.

dates.note: Ends on Sarva Pitru Amavasya / Mahalaya (Oct 10). Some sources start Sep 26 (Purnima shraddh).
Start from a single source; end is the day before Navratri begins. Verify.

rituals.title: Find the tithi
rituals.description: Use the Panchang to find the tithi on which the ancestor passed; for an unknown date use Sarva Pitru Amavasya.

rituals.title: Tarpan
rituals.description: Face south, sit on Kusha asana and offer water mixed with black sesame, barley and flowers to ancestors, reciting their names and gotra.

rituals.title: Pind daan and shraddh
rituals.description: Offer pind (balls of rice/barley, sesame, honey) with a pandit's guidance and perform shraddh.

rituals.title: Panchabali
rituals.description: Set aside food for a cow, dog, crow, ants and gods; then feed Brahmins and give dakshina.

rituals.title: Charity
rituals.description: Donate clothes, grain, umbrellas and food in the names of ancestors.

samagri.name_hi: पिंड सामग्री (जौ/चावल का आटा, तिल, शहद)
पंचबलि भोग (गाय, कुत्ता, कौआ, चींटी, देव)

festivals.significance: Nine nights honouring the nine forms of Durga, culminating in Dussehra.
festivals.how_celebrated: Ghatasthapana on day 1, daily worship of each form, fasting, Garba and Dandiya in Gujarat, Durga Puja in Bengal, Ashtami/Navami kanya pujan.
festivals.traditional_foods: kuttu atta dishes, sabudana, fruits, singhara
festivals.muhurat_rule: Ghatasthapana in the first third of the day or Abhijit Muhurat.
festivals.regional_notes: Garba-dandiya (Gujarat), Durga Puja pandals (Bengal), Ramlila (North), Bathukamma (Telangana); Rajasthan: Mata temples and fairs.

dates.note: Maha Navami Oct 8 per most calendars; one lists Oct 9.

rituals.title: Ghatasthapana setup
rituals.description: Clean the puja space, set a kalash with Ganga water, mango leaves and coconut, and sow barley (jwara) in a pot.

rituals.title: Day 1: Shailputri
rituals.description: Install Ghat at the muhurat, light Akhand Jyot, offer ghee and pure white flowers.

rituals.title: Days 2-9: nine forms
rituals.description: Worship the nine forms daily: Shailputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri, Siddhidatri.

rituals.title: Durga Saptashati path
rituals.description: Read the Durga Saptashati or Devi Mahatmya and chant Navarna mantra.

rituals.title: Ashtami or Navami: havan and kanya pujan
rituals.description: Feed nine girls and a boy, wash their feet, offer halwa-puri-chana and gifts; perform a small havan.

rituals.title: Visarjan
rituals.description: Immerse the idols or Ghat jwara after Dashami puja.

samagri.name_hi: जवारे बोने का पात्र व मिट्टी
samagri.name_en: Pot and soil for jwara (barley sprouts)

samagri.name_hi: कन्या पूजन की भेंट (चुनरी, चूड़ी, फल)

festivals.significance: The final two days of Navratri; Sandhi Puja, kanya pujan and havan are performed.
festivals.how_celebrated: Kanya pujan (feeding nine girls), Durga havan, Ayudha/shastra pujan on Navami.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Sandhi Kaal puja at the Ashtami-Navami junction; havan by Pradosh.
festivals.regional_notes: Bengal's Sandhi Puja; Kota/Jaipur: havan in temples.

dates.note: Ashtami Oct 19, Maha Navami Oct 20.

rituals.title: Sandhi puja
rituals.description: Perform special Sandhi Puja at the transition of Ashtami into Navami with 108 diyas and lotus.

rituals.title: Kanya pujan
rituals.description: Invite nine girls, wash feet, tilak, feed halwa-puri-chana, give chunri and a small gift.

rituals.title: Havan
rituals.description: Perform Durga havan with ghee, havan samagri and a coconut purnahuti.

samagri.name_hi: कन्या पूजन की भेंट (चुनरी, चूड़ी, फल)

festivals.significance: Victory of good over evil: Rama's win over Ravana and Durga's win over Mahishasura.
festivals.how_celebrated: Ravana effigy burning, shastra and Shami pujan, Aparajita puja, Ramlila culmination.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Aparahna (afternoon) puja; effigy burning at dusk.
festivals.regional_notes: Kota Dussehra Mela is famous in Rajasthan; Mysuru Dasara, Kullu Dussehra, Delhi Ramlila.

rituals.title: Shastra pujan
rituals.description: Clean and worship weapons, tools, books and vehicles with roli, flowers and sweets.

rituals.title: Aparajita and Shami puja
rituals.description: Worship Aparajita Devi and Shami tree, take Shami leaves ('sona') and give to elders.

rituals.title: Ravan Dahan
rituals.description: At dusk watch the Ramlila culmination and burning of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad effigies.

rituals.title: Greet and eat
rituals.description: Greet elders, exchange Shami leaves and eat jalebi/fafda or sweets.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: Brightest moon of the year; believed to shower nectar-like rays. Lakshmi is said to bless those awake (Kojagari).
festivals.how_celebrated: Kheer kept under moonlight and eaten as prasad; Lakshmi and Kojagara puja; Raas Leela in Vrindavan.
festivals.regional_notes: Gujarat: Garba; Bengal: Kojagari Lakshmi Puja; North India: kheer in moonlight.

dates.note: Kojagiri night Oct 25; Purnima tithi vrat on Oct 26 per some calendars.

rituals.title: Prepare kheer
rituals.description: Prepare kheer of milk, rice and sugar with dry fruits and keep it covered in a thin cloth.

rituals.title: Moon and Lakshmi puja
rituals.description: After moonrise worship the moon with roli, rice and flowers and perform Lakshmi puja.

rituals.title: Kheer in moonlight
rituals.description: Keep the kheer in an open place in moonlight for several hours.

rituals.title: Prasad
rituals.description: Eat the kheer as prasad after midnight or next morning.

festivals.deity: भगवान शिव, माँ पार्वती, गणेश, चंद्र
festivals.significance: Married women fast for their husbands' longevity and well-being, breaking the fast after sighting the moon.
festivals.how_celebrated: Sargi before dawn, nirjala fast, solah shringar, group katha in the evening, arghya to the moon through a sieve, husband gives first sip.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Evening puja Muhurat and moonrise time (city specific).
festivals.regional_notes: Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, UP, Delhi and MP; moonrise time differs by city.

dates.note: Sources disagree (Oct 28 vs Oct 29); decided by moonrise and Chaturthi at moonrise for your city.

rituals.title: Sargi
rituals.description: Before sunrise eat the sargi prepared by the mother-in-law (fruits, dry fruits, mathri, sweets) and drink water.

rituals.title: Nirjala fast
rituals.description: Observe the fast without water and food through the day; get ready with solah shringar by evening.

rituals.title: Karwa puja and katha
rituals.description: In the evening gather with other women, worship Shiva-Parvati and Ganesha, exchange karwa and listen to the Karwa Chauth katha.

rituals.title: Moon arghya
rituals.description: After moonrise view the moon through a sieve, offer water in a lota, then look at the husband through the sieve.

rituals.title: Break the fast
rituals.description: Husband offers the first sip of water and first bite of food; eat dinner together.

festivals.significance: Mothers fast for children's well-being; Ahoi Mata is worshipped at dusk.
festivals.how_celebrated: Ahoi Mata drawn or hung on the wall, evening katha, arghya to stars (or moon) to break the fast.
festivals.regional_notes: North India (UP, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana).

rituals.title: Ahoi Mata image
rituals.description: Draw Ahoi Mata with her cubs on the wall or place a printed picture and silver Ahoi pendant.

rituals.title: Evening puja and katha
rituals.description: At dusk offer roli, akshat, halwa-puri and listen to the Ahoi Ashtami katha.

rituals.title: Break the fast
rituals.description: After sighting stars (or the moon in some traditions) offer arghya and break the fast; give the pendant a thread of 'moli'.

festivals.significance: First day of Diwali; Dhanvantari, the physician of the gods, emerged with the nectar pot. Buying metals or utensils is auspicious.
festivals.how_celebrated: Puja of Dhanvantari, Lakshmi and Kuber at Pradosh; buying gold, silver, utensils; Yamadeep Daan (a lamp for Yama) in the evening.
festivals.regional_notes: Jaipur's jewellery and Johari Bazaar markets are packed; many buy brooms and kitchenware.

rituals.title: Buy something new
rituals.description: Buy gold, silver, a new utensil or broom during the day; avoid iron/black items by local custom.

rituals.title: Dhanvantari and Lakshmi puja
rituals.description: In Pradosh Kaal place Dhanvantari, Lakshmi-Ganesh and Kuber; offer flowers, dhaniya-gud, sweets.

rituals.title: Light a Yamadeep
rituals.description: After sunset light a four-faced oil diya outside the main door facing south for Yama to protect from untimely death.

rituals.title: Lamp tradition
rituals.description: Keep 13 diyas lit around the home as many families do on Dhanteras night.

festivals.significance: Krishna's victory over the demon Narakasura; Abhyang Snan (oil bath) before sunrise is said to remove sins.
festivals.how_celebrated: Abhyang snan with ubtan and til oil before sunrise, evening diyas, worship of Yama and Hanuman (Kali Chaudas).
festivals.muhurat_rule: Abhyang snan during the Chandrodaya-Sunrise window.
festivals.regional_notes: Roop Chaudas in Rajasthan/Gujarat; Kali Chaudas in Gujarat and Bengal (Kali puja at night).

dates.note: Abhyang snan on Nov 8 morning; Kali Chaudas night observance on Nov 7 in some regions.

rituals.title: Abhyang snan
rituals.description: Before sunrise apply ubtan and til oil, then bathe; this is said to remove sins and bring health.

rituals.title: Worship Yama and Krishna
rituals.description: Offer lamps to Yama, remember Krishna's victory over Narakasura, and in Gujarat/Bengal worship Kali or Hanuman at night.

rituals.title: Evening diyas
rituals.description: Light many diyas at home at dusk, a start of the Diwali lighting.

festivals.significance: Festival of lights marking Rama's return to Ayodhya and the worship of Lakshmi, goddess of wealth.
festivals.how_celebrated: Home cleaning and rangoli, lighting diyas, Lakshmi-Ganesh puja at Pradosh, chopda pujan in shops, sweets exchange, fireworks.
festivals.traditional_foods: laddu, kaju katli, gujiya, mathri, khil-batasha
festivals.muhurat_rule: Pradosh Kaal with Sthir Lagna (Vrishabha) is best; Nishita Kaal for Tantric puja.
festivals.regional_notes: Jaipur markets (Bapu Bazaar, Johari Bazaar) are lit up for Diwali; Gujarati New Year follows; Bengal: Kali Puja.

dates.note: Lakshmi Puja on Nov 8.
Most calendars list Oct 29; one lists Oct 28.

rituals.title: Clean and decorate
rituals.description: Clean the home, make rangoli at the entrance, hang toran of mango leaves and marigold, keep diyas ready.

rituals.title: Fix the muhurat
rituals.description: Check the Lakshmi Puja Muhurat (Pradosh Kaal with Sthir Lagna) for your city.

rituals.title: Set up the puja chowki
rituals.description: Spread a red cloth on a chowki, place Lakshmi-Ganesh idols, install a kalash with mango leaves and a coconut, and keep silver coins and account books nearby.

rituals.title: Sankalp and Ganesh puja
rituals.description: Take sankalp with water and rice, invoke Ganesha first with roli, akshat, durva and modak.

rituals.title: Lakshmi puja
rituals.description: Offer panchamrit, kumkum, lotus, khil-batasha and sweets to Lakshmi; chant Shri Suktam or Lakshmi mantras; also worship Kuber and Saraswati.

rituals.title: Aarti
rituals.description: Perform aarti with a ghee diya and camphor, ring the bell and distribute prasad.

rituals.title: Light diyas
rituals.description: Light diyas at the main door, courtyard, kitchen and windows; share sweets with family and neighbours.

rituals.title: Chopda pujan (business)
rituals.description: Traders worship account books and cash box and open new ledgers.

festivals.significance: Krishna lifted Govardhan hill to shelter Vrindavan from Indra's rain; Annakut offers a mountain of food.
festivals.how_celebrated: Cow-dung Govardhan figure circled and worshipped, Annakut (56 bhog) offered, cows decorated.
festivals.traditional_foods: annakut, kadhi, bajre ki roti, sweets
festivals.regional_notes: Mathura-Vrindavan, Nathdwara (Rajasthan), Jaipur Govind Dev Ji temple; Gujarati New Year (Bestu Varas).

dates.note: Gujarati New Year listed Nov 10 by some calendars.

rituals.title: Make the Govardhan figure
rituals.description: Make a reclining Govardhan mountain from cow dung in the courtyard and decorate with flowers.

rituals.title: Worship
rituals.description: Offer roli, akshat, kheer, dahi and Annakut (a mountain of cooked food), then circumambulate the figure.

rituals.title: Cow puja
rituals.description: Bathe and decorate cows, feed them and worship them.

rituals.title: Share Annakut
rituals.description: Distribute the Annakut prasad among family and the neighbourhood.

festivals.significance: Sisters pray for brothers' long life; Yama visited his sister Yamuna on this day.
festivals.how_celebrated: Tilak on the brother's forehead, aarti, sweets; brother gives gifts.
festivals.regional_notes: Bhau Beej (Maharashtra), Bhai Phonta (Bengal).

rituals.title: Prepare tilak thali
rituals.description: Sister prepares a thali with roli, akshat, a lamp, sweets and a coconut gola.

rituals.title: Tilak and aarti
rituals.description: Sister applies tilak, performs aarti of the brother, and feeds him sweets and mishri.

rituals.title: Gifts and promise
rituals.description: Brother gives a gift and promises to protect and support her.

festivals.significance: Four-day Sun worship from Bihar, UP and Jharkhand for family well-being.
festivals.how_celebrated: Nahay-Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya at sunset, Usha Arghya at sunrise at river or pond banks with bamboo soop offerings.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Exact sunset and sunrise times of your city.
festivals.regional_notes: Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern UP, Delhi and diaspora.

dates.note: Sandhya Arghya (main day) on Nov 15; Nahay-Khay Nov 13, Kharna Nov 14, Usha Arghya Nov 16 (derived from main day).
Main day (Sandhya Arghya); other days to be derived.

rituals.title: Day 1: Nahay-Khay
rituals.description: Bathe in a river or clean water, cook a pure meal of kaddu (bottle gourd), chana dal and rice and eat once.

rituals.title: Day 2: Kharna
rituals.description: Fast all day; in the evening eat kheer, roti and fruit prasad; then the 36-hour nirjala fast starts.

rituals.title: Day 3: Sandhya Arghya
rituals.description: Go to the river or pond bank, stand in water and offer arghya to the setting Sun with fruits, thekua and bamboo soop.

rituals.title: Day 4: Usha Arghya
rituals.description: Before sunrise offer arghya to the rising Sun and break the fast with prasad (parana).

festivals.significance: Vishnu wakes after four months of sleep (Chaturmas); weddings and auspicious work resume.
festivals.how_celebrated: Fast, Vishnu puja, sugarcane mandap in the courtyard, chants of 'Uthho Dev' and Tulsi Vivah preparations.
festivals.regional_notes: North India, Maharashtra (Kartiki Ekadashi, Pandharpur).

rituals.title: Make the courtyard design
rituals.description: Draw Vishnu's footprints or a rangoli in the courtyard with rice paste and place a sugarcane mandap.

rituals.title: Fast and Vishnu puja
rituals.description: Offer tulsi, fruits, singhara, sugarcane and panchamrit to Vishnu.

rituals.title: Wake the God
rituals.description: Ring bells and chant 'Uthho Dev, baitho Dev, angurhiyan chatkao Dev'.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast the next morning during the Parana window.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: Ceremonial marriage of Tulsi with Shaligram (Vishnu) marking the start of wedding season.
festivals.how_celebrated: Tulsi decorated as a bride with chunri and shringar, mandap of sugarcane, pheras with Shaligram, aarti.
festivals.regional_notes: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and UP.

rituals.title: Decorate Tulsi
rituals.description: Tulsi plant is decorated with a chunri, bindi, bangles and a sugarcane mandap.

rituals.title: Shaligram on a chowki
rituals.description: Keep a Shaligram or Vishnu image on a chowki as the bridegroom.

rituals.title: Vivah ritual
rituals.description: Perform kanyadaan, haldi, sindoor and pheras around Tulsi chanting mangalashtak, then aarti.

rituals.title: Prasad
rituals.description: Distribute sweets and amla; the wedding season begins.

festivals.significance: Holy full moon of Kartik: Ganga snan, deepdan and Shiva's victory over Tripurasura.
festivals.how_celebrated: Holy dip, deepdan with thousands of diyas on ghats, Satyanarayan katha.
festivals.regional_notes: Varanasi's Dev Deepawali, Pushkar Fair and holy dip in Rajasthan, Guru Nanak Jayanti.

dates.note: Dev Diwali.
Dev Diwali.

rituals.title: Holy dip
rituals.description: Take a Kartik snan before sunrise in a holy river or pond (Pushkar, Ganga, Yamuna).

rituals.title: Deepdan
rituals.description: Light diyas at the ghats or home in the evening and float lamps in the river.

rituals.title: Satyanarayan katha
rituals.description: Perform Satyanarayan puja and katha and donate.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: Birth anniversary of the first Sikh Guru, Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
festivals.how_celebrated: Akhand Path, nagar kirtan processions, langar and gurdwara decoration.
festivals.regional_notes: Punjab, Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan; Nankana Sahib (Pakistan).

dates.note: Kartik Purnima; verify.

rituals.title: Prabhat pheri
rituals.description: Early morning kirtan processions through localities.

rituals.title: Akhand Path and nagar kirtan
rituals.description: Continuous recitation of Guru Granth Sahib and Nagar Kirtan procession.

rituals.title: Langar
rituals.description: Community meal with karah prasad.

festivals.significance: Birth of Kalabhairava, the fierce form of Shiva, protector of time and travelers.
festivals.how_celebrated: Night puja, mustard-oil lamp, offering black sesame and urad, feeding dogs, Bhairav Chalisa.
festivals.regional_notes: Ujjain Kal Bhairav temple, Varanasi Kal Bhairav.

rituals.title: Night puja
rituals.description: Offer a mustard-oil diya, black sesame, urad dishes and jalebi to Kal Bhairav; recite Bhairav Chalisa.

rituals.title: Feed dogs
rituals.description: Feed dogs and give daan to the poor.

festivals.deity: भगवान श्री राम और माता सीता
festivals.significance: Marriage anniversary of Rama and Sita, celebrated especially in Ayodhya, Janakpur and Mithila.
festivals.how_celebrated: Ram-Sita vivah rituals, Ramcharitmanas path, bhajans.
festivals.regional_notes: Janakpur (Nepal), Ayodhya; many avoid wedding on this day in Mithila.

rituals.title: Sita-Ram vivah
rituals.description: Decorate a picture of Sita-Ram, offer shringar and sweets, and sing wedding songs and recite Vivah Prasang of Ramcharitmanas.

festivals.significance: The day Krishna taught the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the Kurukshetra battlefield; coincides with Mokshada Ekadashi.
festivals.how_celebrated: Gita path, discourses, Vishnu puja, fast.
festivals.regional_notes: Kurukshetra celebrates with an international Gita Mahotsav.

dates.note: Mokshada Ekadashi.

rituals.title: Gita path
rituals.description: Recite the Bhagavad Gita or at least a few chapters and offer tulsi to Krishna.

rituals.title: Fast and charity
rituals.description: Observe the Ekadashi fast and donate.

festivals.significance: Kerala's harvest festival welcoming King Mahabali.
festivals.how_celebrated: Pookalam floral carpets, Onasadya feast, boat races, Kathakali, Pulikali.
festivals.regional_notes: Kerala and Malayali diaspora.

dates.note: Thiruvonam.

rituals.title: Pookalam and Onasadya
rituals.description: Make a floral carpet at the entrance and serve a banquet with banana leaf.

rituals.title: Celebrations
rituals.description: Join boat races, Pulikali, Kaikottikali.

festivals.significance: The eleventh tithi of each fortnight is dedicated to Vishnu; fasting without grains is believed to cleanse mind and body.
festivals.how_celebrated: Fast, Vishnu and Tulsi puja, Vishnu Sahasranama, parana next morning.
festivals.muhurat_rule: Parana in the Dwadashi window next morning.
festivals.regional_notes: Observed by Vaishnavas across India; 24 per year (26 in an Adhik Maas year).

rituals.title: Dashami
rituals.description: Eat sattvic food once on Dashami (avoid grains and rice on Ekadashi).

rituals.title: Fast and puja
rituals.description: Worship Vishnu with tulsi, Panchamrit and yellow flowers; read the Ekadashi katha.

rituals.title: Parana
rituals.description: Break the fast next morning in the Parana window with grain food first offered to Vishnu.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: Full-moon day observed with Satyanarayan katha, moon worship and holy dips.
festivals.how_celebrated: Fast, Satyanarayan katha with panchamrit and sooji halwa prasad, moon arghya.
festivals.regional_notes: Widely observed in Gujarat, Rajasthan, UP and Maharashtra.

rituals.title: Satyanarayan katha
rituals.description: Install Satyanarayan image on a chowki with banana pillars, perform kalash puja, read five chapters of the katha and offer sooji halwa and Panchamrit prasad.

rituals.title: Moon arghya
rituals.description: Offer arghya to the moon in the evening.

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

festivals.significance: New-moon day dedicated to ancestors (tarpan), Shani, and spiritual practices.
festivals.how_celebrated: Pitru tarpan, daan, holy dips, Shani puja on Saturdays.
festivals.regional_notes: Somvati and Mauni Amavasya are particularly significant.

rituals.title: Tarpan and daan
rituals.description: Offer water with black sesame to ancestors, light a diya under a peepal tree, and donate food and clothes.

festivals.significance: Shiva worshipped at twilight on Trayodashi of both pakshas.
festivals.how_celebrated: Fast, evening abhishek, bel patra, Shiva aarti.
festivals.regional_notes: Somvar Pradosh and Shani Pradosh are special.

rituals.title: Shiva abhishek
rituals.description: At twilight perform abhishek with milk, curd, honey and gangajal, offer bel patra, light a diya and recite Shiva Chalisa and aarti.

festivals.significance: Monthly Chaturthi fast for Ganesha, broken after moonrise.
festivals.how_celebrated: Fast, Ganesh puja with durva and modak, moon arghya.
festivals.regional_notes: Angarki Chaturthi (Tuesday) is the most auspicious.

rituals.title: Ganesh puja
rituals.description: Worship Ganesha with durva, modak and red flowers, and read the Sankashti katha.

rituals.title: Moon arghya
rituals.description: After moonrise offer arghya and break the fast.

poojas.description: Worship of Lord Vishnu as Satyanarayan with a five-chapter katha, done on Purnima or any auspicious occasion.
poojas.best_for: Purnima, new home, new business, wishes fulfilled
poojas.muhurat_rule: Evening or morning on a Purnima or auspicious day

samagri.name_hi: विष्णु / सत्यनारायण जी की मूर्ति / चित्र

poojas.description: Fire ritual with mantras and ghee/samagri offerings to deities; used for shanti, festivals and vastu.
poojas.muhurat_rule: Pandit picks muhurat; avoid Bhadra and Rahu Kaal

poojas.description: Housewarming ceremony with Ganesh puja, Vastu puja, havan and milk boiling in the new home.
poojas.muhurat_rule: Choose an auspicious Panchang date (avoid Chaturmas and Adhik Maas)

poojas.description: Abhishek of Shivling with milk, water, curd, honey and ghee while chanting Sri Rudram.
poojas.best_for: Shivratri, Sawan Somvar, Pradosh, health and peace

poojas.description: Appeasement of the nine planets with kalash, mantras and havan.
poojas.best_for: Graha dosha as per horoscope, new ventures
poojas.muhurat_rule: Pandit chooses tithi and nakshatra per horoscope

samagri.name_hi: नवग्रह के नौ रंगों के वस्त्र

poojas.description: Basic puja of Ganesha before any ritual or on Ganesh Chaturthi / Sankashti.
Worship of Lakshmi and Ganesha for wealth and prosperity at Diwali, Dhanteras or new business.
poojas.muhurat_rule: Pradosh Kaal with Sthir Lagna on Diwali

poojas.description: Recitation of the 700 verses of Devi Mahatmya with Ghatasthapana in Navratri.

samagri.name_hi: जवारे बोने का पात्र व मिट्टी
samagri.name_en: Pot and soil for jwara (barley sprouts)

poojas.description: Recitation of Sundarkand from Ramcharitmanas to Hanuman for strength and relief from fears.
Non-stop recitation of Ramcharitmanas over about 24 hours.
poojas.muhurat_rule: Start at an auspicious morning hour

poojas.description: Ritual remembrance of ancestors with tarpan, pind daan and Brahmin bhojan.

poojas.description: Wedding rites: Ganesh puja, kanyadaan, havan, saptapadi and sindoor.
poojas.muhurat_rule: Fix wedding muhurat from kundali matching

poojas.description: First haircut ceremony of a child with puja and havan.
poojas.muhurat_rule: Auspicious tithi and nakshatra, avoid Chaturmas

poojas.description: Naming ceremony with puja, rashi-based name selection and blessings.
poojas.muhurat_rule: Day and nakshatra chosen by pandit

poojas.description: Foundation laying puja before construction starts.

poojas.description: Rituals to harmonise the space before or after entering a building.

poojas.description: Chanting of the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra for health and protection.
Worship of Saraswati for knowledge and arts, also Vidyarambh.
Worship of nine girls as forms of Durga on Ashtami or Navami.
